name: Barbell back squat
form_cues: Bar sits on your upper traps, hands just outside shoulders
Brace hard, then sit down between your heels
Drive up through mid-foot, chest and hips rising together
common_mistakes: Cutting depth short as the weight climbs
safety: Squat inside a rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
notes: Add a 2–3 sec pause at the bottom for a tougher, technique-focused variation.

name: Low-bar back squat
form_cues: Rest the bar on the shelf of your rear delts, below the traps
Push hips back and lean your chest forward more than high-bar
Keep wrists straight and elbows driving up out of the hole
common_mistakes: Wrists bent back taking the load
Turning the lift into a good morning
safety: Use safety pins and warm your shoulders up first; stop if elbows or wrists ache.
notes: Common in powerlifting because the shorter lever lets you move more weight.

name: Front squat
form_cues: Rest the bar on your front delts with elbows high
Keep your torso upright as you sit straight down
Lead with the elbows as you drive up
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping and bar rolling forward
safety: Use safety pins; if the bar slips forward, push it away and step back.
notes: Use a cross-arm grip or straps if wrist mobility limits the clean grip.

name: Barbell box squat
form_cues: Set a box at or just below parallel
Sit back until you lightly touch the box, staying tight
Drive up hard without rocking off the box
safety: Never drop onto the box under load; sit with control.
notes: Great for teaching depth and hip drive, and easier on the knees.

name: Zercher squat
form_cues: Cradle the bar in the crooks of your elbows, hands together
Stay tall and brace as you squat between your knees
Keep elbows up so the bar doesn't drag you forward
common_mistakes: Going too heavy before the arms adapt
safety: Pad the bar or wear long sleeves; set the rack hooks at mid-chest height.
notes: Builds a strong upper back and brace; a favourite of strongmen.

name: Overhead squat
form_cues: Lock the bar overhead with a wide snatch grip
Push up into the bar and keep it over mid-foot
Sit straight down with your chest tall
safety: Practise with an empty bar; learn to dump the bar forward or back safely.
notes: A key snatch accessory that builds overhead stability and mobility.

name: Safety squat bar squat
form_cues: Hold the handles lightly and keep elbows down
Brace and fight to keep your chest up
Sit down between your heels and drive straight up
common_mistakes: Letting the bar tip you forward
safety: Use safety pins; the bar's camber pushes you forward, so start lighter than your back squat.
notes: Needs a safety squat bar (no app gear id; nearest is barbell). Shoulder-friendly squat option.

name: Anderson squat
form_cues: Set the pins at your sticking point and start under the bar
Get tight and brace before you push
Drive the bar off the pins without bouncing
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the pins
safety: Pins must be secure and level; lower each rep back to the pins with control.
notes: Starts from a dead stop to build strength out of the bottom.

name: Barbell hack squat
form_cues: Hold the bar behind your legs, arms straight
Squat down keeping your chest up and the bar close
Stand tall by pushing through the whole foot
common_mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom
safety: Raise the plates on small blocks if the bar hits your heels.
notes: Different from the machine hack squat; great quad builder with just a barbell.

name: Barbell split squat
form_cues: Take a long split stance with feet hip-width apart
Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor
Push through the front foot to rise
common_mistakes: Feet in a straight line, causing wobble
safety: Start light to find balance; unrack and rerack with both feet together.

name: Barbell Bulgarian split squat
form_cues: Rest the back foot laces-down on a bench
Lower straight down until the back knee nearly touches
Drive up through the front heel
common_mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench
safety: Master the dumbbell version first; balance is the limiter with a bar on your back.

name: Barbell reverse lunge
form_cues: Step back far enough that the front shin stays fairly upright
Lower the back knee under control
Push off the front foot to return to standing
common_mistakes: Short step putting pressure on the front knee
safety: Use a lighter load than your squat and keep the area around you clear.
notes: Usually kinder on the knees than forward lunges.

name: Barbell forward lunge
form_cues: Step forward and land heel first
Drop the back knee straight down
Push firmly back to the start
common_mistakes: Knee shooting far past toes with heel lifting
safety: Requires good balance and deceleration; start with an empty bar.

name: Barbell walking lunge
form_cues: Take long, steady steps with feet hip-width apart
Lightly kiss the back knee to the floor
Drive through the front foot into the next step
safety: Need a clear path; set the bar down if you lose balance rather than fighting it.

name: Barbell lateral lunge
form_cues: Step wide to the side and sit back into that hip
Keep the trailing leg straight and both feet flat
Push off the bent leg to return
common_mistakes: Knee caving in on the working leg
safety: Go light; the side-to-side load is harder to control under a bar.

name: Barbell step-up
form_cues: Plant your whole foot on a knee-height box
Drive up through the top heel, not the back toe
Lower slowly to the floor
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the bottom leg
safety: Use a sturdy, non-slip box and keep the height modest when loaded.

name: Barbell standing calf raise
form_cues: Stand tall with the bar on your back
Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet
Lower slowly to a full stretch
safety: Stand on a plate edge for more range only once balance is solid.

name: Barbell jump squat
form_cues: Use a light bar, around 20–30% of your squat
Dip quickly and jump as high as you can
Land softly and reset before the next rep
safety: Hold the bar tightly to your back; stop if your landings get sloppy.
notes: Trap bar jumps are safer for most people.

name: Deadlift
form_cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins close, hands just outside legs
Pull the slack out, brace, then push the floor away
Lock out by squeezing glutes, not leaning back
common_mistakes: Bar drifting away from the legs
Jerking the bar off the floor
safety: Keep a neutral spine; use bumper plates or pads if you might drop it.
notes: Reset each rep for cleaner technique.

name: Sumo deadlift
form_cues: Take a wide stance with toes turned out, hands inside the knees
Push knees out over the toes and keep chest up
Spread the floor with your feet and stand tall
common_mistakes: Hips rising before the bar moves
Stance so wide you can't push
safety: Warm up hips and adductors well before heavy sets.

name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Start standing and soften the knees slightly
Push your hips back, sliding the bar down your thighs
Stop when hamstrings are stretched, then drive hips forward
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower
Bending the knees into a squat
Bar drifting away from the legs
safety: Only go as low as you can keep a flat back.

name: Stiff-leg deadlift
form_cues: Start from the floor with knees nearly straight
Hinge at the hips with a long, flat back
Pull the bar up close to your legs
safety: Use a weight you can control with a flat back; skip if you have a lower-back injury.
notes: Unlike the RDL, each rep starts from the floor.

name: Deficit deadlift
form_cues: Stand on a 2–5 cm platform or plate
Set your hips a little lower than a normal deadlift
Push the floor away and keep the bar close
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the bar
safety: Use a stable platform; reduce weight by about 10–20% versus your regular pull.
notes: Builds speed and strength off the floor.

name: Rack pull
form_cues: Set the bar on pins just below or above the knee
Wedge into the bar and brace before pulling
Finish tall with glutes squeezed and shoulders back
common_mistakes: Using it as an ego lift with poor form
safety: Lower the bar under control so it doesn't bounce on the pins.
notes: Can also be done off blocks.

name: Snatch-grip deadlift
form_cues: Take a wide snatch grip with hips set lower than usual
Keep your chest up and the bar close
Push through the floor, squeezing the upper back
safety: Use straps if grip fails before the back; start lighter than your deadlift.

name: Good morning
form_cues: Bar on upper traps, knees softly bent
Push hips back and bow forward with a flat back
Stop at about parallel and drive hips forward
safety: Start very light; stop the descent the moment your back starts to round.

name: Seated good morning
form_cues: Sit astride a bench with the bar on your upper back
Lean forward from the hips with a flat back
Rise back up by squeezing glutes and back
safety: Light loads only; skip if you have lower-back problems.

name: Barbell hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on the bench edge, bar padded over your hips
Tuck your chin and drive through your heels
Squeeze glutes hard at the top with shins vertical
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Feet too far away or too close
safety: Always use a pad or folded mat under the bar.

name: Barbell glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back, bar padded across your hips
Plant feet close and drive hips up
Pause and squeeze at the top
safety: Pad the bar; use bumper plates so the bar can roll over your legs.
notes: Shorter range than the hip thrust but easier to set up.

name: Barbell bench press
form_cues: Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades pinched, feet planted
Lower the bar to your mid-chest with elbows at about 45°
Press up and slightly back over your shoulders
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
safety: Use a spotter or safety arms; never use a thumbless grip.

name: Incline barbell press
form_cues: Set the bench to 30–45°
Lower the bar to your upper chest
Press up over your shoulders, shoulder blades tucked
safety: Use a spotter or safeties; keep your back pinned to the pad.

name: Decline bench press
form_cues: Lock your legs under the pads
Lower the bar to your lower chest
Press straight up over your shoulders
safety: Always use a spotter; it's hard to bail out of a decline press.

name: Close-grip bench press
form_cues: Grip about shoulder-width, not much closer
Keep elbows tucked near your sides
Touch the lower chest and press to lockout
common_mistakes: Hands so close it hurts the wrists
safety: Use a spotter; wrists should stay stacked over elbows.

name: Wide-grip bench press
form_cues: Grip about one-and-a-half times shoulder-width
Lower under control to mid-chest
Press up without letting shoulders roll forward
common_mistakes: Going wider than the rings allow
safety: Avoid if you have shoulder pain; stay within competition grip width (index finger on the rings).
notes: Shorter range and more chest emphasis than a standard grip.

name: Reverse-grip bench press
form_cues: Take an underhand grip just outside shoulder-width
Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows tucked
Press back toward your face in an arc
safety: Always use a spotter for the hand-off; the grip is easy to lose.

name: Barbell floor press
form_cues: Lie under the bar in a rack with knees bent
Lower until your upper arms rest on the floor
Pause, then press back to lockout
safety: Set rack pins low enough to unrack, and use safeties.
notes: Shoulder-friendly; good lockout builder.

name: Pin press
form_cues: Set pins just above your chest or at a sticking point
Get tight under the bar before every rep
Press explosively off the pins
common_mistakes: Bench not centred in the rack
safety: Make sure the pins are level and the bench is centred.
notes: Builds strength from a dead stop.

name: Barbell pullover
form_cues: Lie on a bench holding the bar over your chest, elbows soft
Lower it back over your head in an arc
Pull it back over your chest using lats and chest
safety: Use a light load and stop if your shoulders pinch overhead.

name: Landmine squeeze press
form_cues: Hold the bar end with both palms pressed together
Squeeze your hands hard into the bar
Press up and out from your chest
safety: Keep the landmine anchored so it can't slide.

name: Standing barbell overhead press
form_cues: Bar on front delts, hands just outside shoulders
Squeeze glutes, move your head back and press straight up
Push your head through at the top
common_mistakes: Leaning back and turning it into an incline press
Pressing the bar around the face
safety: Keep ribs down to protect your lower back.

name: Seated barbell overhead press
form_cues: Set the bench upright, back against the pad
Lower the bar to your upper chest
Press straight up past your face
safety: Use a rack or spotter for unracking.

name: Behind-the-neck press
form_cues: Take a wider grip with the bar on your traps
Press straight up with head neutral
Lower only as far as shoulders comfortably allow
safety: Only for people with good shoulder mobility and no shoulder pain.
notes: Also useful as a jerk accessory for weightlifters.

name: Z press
form_cues: Sit on the floor with legs straight out in front
Brace hard and press the bar straight up
Keep your torso tall without leaning back
safety: Set the rack low so you can unrack seated; use light weights.
notes: Removes the legs and lower back from the press, exposing weak spots.

name: Barbell front raise
form_cues: Hold the bar at your thighs, shoulder-width grip
Raise it to eye level with soft elbows
Lower slowly, no swinging
safety: Keep it light; the long lever stresses the shoulders.

name: Barbell upright row
form_cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders
Lead with your elbows up to chest height
Lower slowly
safety: Stop at chest height and skip it if you feel shoulder pinching.

name: Barbell shrug
form_cues: Hold the bar at your thighs, arms straight
Lift your shoulders straight up to your ears
Pause, then lower slowly
safety: Use straps for heavy sets to spare your grip.

name: Behind-the-back barbell shrug
form_cues: Hold the bar behind your thighs
Shrug up and slightly back
Hold the top for a second
safety: Unrack from mid-thigh height in a rack.

name: Barbell bent-over row
form_cues: Hinge until your torso is about 45° or lower
Pull the bar to your lower ribs
Lower under control without standing up
safety: Keep your back flat; stop if your lower back fatigues first.

name: Pendlay row
form_cues: Start each rep with the bar on the floor, back flat
Torso near parallel to the floor
Pull explosively to your lower chest, then set it down
common_mistakes: Not resting the bar each rep
safety: Needs good hamstring mobility to keep a flat back.

name: Underhand barbell row
form_cues: Underhand grip, shoulder-width
Lean over to about 70°
Pull the bar to your belly button
safety: Avoid if supinated grip bothers your elbows.

name: Seal row
form_cues: Lie chest-down on a raised bench
Pull the bar to the underside of the bench
Lower to full stretch
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
safety: Bench must be stable and raised on blocks or a frame.
notes: Removes the lower back from rowing. Needs a raised bench (no specific gear id).

name: T-bar row
form_cues: Straddle the bar and hinge to about 45°
Pull the handle to your chest
Lower slowly to full stretch
safety: Keep your back flat; use a V-handle under the bar.
notes: The machine version needs only the tbar gear.

name: Meadows row
form_cues: Stand side-on to the bar end and stagger your stance
Grip the thick end overhand
Pull your elbow up and back
safety: Rest your free forearm on your knee for support.

name: Barbell curl
form_cues: Hands shoulder-width, elbows tucked
Curl without swinging
Lower slowly to full extension
safety: Stop if your wrists hurt; switch to an EZ bar.

name: EZ-bar curl
form_cues: Grip the angled handles
Keep elbows by your sides
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly
safety: Wrist-friendlier than a straight bar.

name: Reverse barbell curl
form_cues: Overhand grip, shoulder-width
Curl while keeping wrists straight
Lower slowly
safety: Use an EZ bar if the straight bar hurts the wrists.

name: Drag curl
form_cues: Pull your elbows back as you curl
Drag the bar up your torso
Lower the same path
safety: Use moderate weights.

name: Preacher curl
form_cues: Armpits snug on the pad
Curl up without lifting elbows
Lower to nearly straight arms
safety: Don't lock out hard at the bottom under heavy loads.

name: EZ-bar spider curl
form_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench
Let arms hang straight down
Curl up and squeeze hard
safety: Use light weight; can also use dumbbells.

name: EZ-bar skull crusher
form_cues: Lie on a bench, bar over your eyes
Lower the bar to your forehead by bending elbows
Extend back without moving upper arms
safety: Control the bar; use a spotter if heavy.
notes: Can be done with a straight bar too.

name: EZ-bar overhead triceps extension
form_cues: Hold the bar overhead, elbows pointed forward
Lower behind your head
Extend back up
safety: Sit on a bench for support if needed.

name: JM press
form_cues: Grip close and tuck elbows
Lower bar toward your chin
Press back up
safety: Learn with an empty bar and a spotter.
notes: A hybrid between a close-grip bench and a skull crusher.

name: Barbell reverse wrist curl
form_cues: Rest forearms on a bench, palms down
Lift the back of your hands up
Lower slowly
safety: Light loads; good for elbow health.

name: Behind-the-back barbell wrist curl
form_cues: Hold the bar behind your thighs
Curl your wrists up
Lower to fingertips
safety: Unrack from a rack at hip height.

name: Trap bar deadlift
form_cues: Stand in the centre of the bar, handles in line with your ankles
Sit hips down and grip the handles
Push the floor away and stand tall
safety: Easier on the lower back than a straight bar; still keep a neutral spine.
notes: Use the high handles to shorten the range for beginners.

name: Trap bar Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Start standing, knees soft
Push your hips back as the bar slides down
Stop at a hamstring stretch and stand back up
safety: Only go as low as you can keep a flat back.

name: Trap bar shrug
form_cues: Stand in the bar with arms straight
Shrug straight up to your ears
Pause and lower slowly
safety: Use straps for heavy sets.
notes: Neutral grip keeps the load at your sides like dumbbells.

name: Trap bar jump
form_cues: Use about 20–30% of your trap bar deadlift
Dip quickly and jump as high as possible
Land softly, reset and repeat
safety: Land with soft knees and keep the bar under control.

name: Landmine press
form_cues: Hold the bar end at your shoulder
Press up and forward
Lower slowly back to the shoulder
safety: Shoulder-friendly; keep your ribs down.
notes: Do it half-kneeling or standing.

name: Landmine squat
form_cues: Hold the bar end at your chest
Sit down between your heels
Drive up through mid-foot
safety: Good beginner squat; the arc supports the torso.

name: Landmine thruster
form_cues: Squat with the bar end at your chest
Drive up and press in one motion
Lower back to the chest
safety: Moderate loads; keep your core braced.

name: Single-leg landmine Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Hold the bar end in the opposite hand
Hinge on one leg, reaching the other leg back
Return by driving hips forward
safety: The landmine offers extra stability.

name: Landmine reverse lunge
form_cues: Hold the bar end at your chest
Step back and lower the knee
Drive through the front foot to stand
safety: Stable loading for beginners.

name: Landmine lateral raise
form_cues: Stand side-on, holding the bar end low across your body
Raise it out to shoulder height
Lower slowly
safety: Light loads.

name: Smith machine squat
form_cues: Feet slightly in front of the bar
Sit down under control
Drive up through mid-foot
safety: Set the safety stops just below your bottom position.

name: Smith machine bench press
form_cues: Line the bar up with your mid-chest
Lower under control
Press up and lock out
safety: Set safety stops above your chest.

name: Smith machine incline bench press
form_cues: Set the bench at 30–45°
Lower to your upper chest
Press straight up
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Smith machine shoulder press
form_cues: Sit upright with the bar just in front of your face
Lower to chin level
Press up to lockout
safety: Set the bench so the bar clears your face.

name: Smith machine bent-over row
form_cues: Hinge to about 45°
Pull the bar to your lower ribs
Lower slowly
safety: Keep a flat back.

name: Smith machine shrug
form_cues: Stand tall with arms straight
Shrug straight up
Pause and lower
safety: Use straps if needed.

name: Smith machine Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Stand close with feet under the bar
Push hips back keeping the bar close
Stand up by driving hips forward
safety: Only go as low as your back stays flat.

name: Smith machine hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on the bench
Bar over the hips, padded
Drive hips up and squeeze
safety: Pad the bar.

name: Smith machine split squat
form_cues: Long split stance under the bar
Lower the back knee
Push up through the front foot
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Smith machine Bulgarian split squat
form_cues: Rear foot on a bench
Lower straight down
Drive up through the front heel
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Smith machine calf raise
form_cues: Stand on a plate
Rise high on your toes
Lower to a full stretch
safety: Use a stable step.

name: Smith machine close-grip bench press
form_cues: Shoulder-width grip
Tuck elbows
Press to lockout
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Smith machine reverse lunge
form_cues: Step back under the bar
Lower the back knee
Drive back to standing
safety: Stable option for beginners.

name: Snatch
form_cues: Wide grip, bar over mid-foot, chest up and back flat
Push the floor away, then explode through hips and knees
Pull yourself under and catch in a deep overhead squat
common_mistakes: Bar swinging away from the body
safety: Learn from a qualified coach and use bumper plates on a platform; drop the bar forward if you miss.

name: Power snatch
form_cues: Start like a snatch with a wide grip
Extend fully, then pull under fast
Catch above parallel with arms locked
common_mistakes: Starting the pull too fast off the floor
safety: Use bumpers and a clear platform; miss by pushing the bar away and stepping back.

name: Hang snatch
form_cues: Start standing, lower the bar to just above the knees
Stay over the bar, then extend explosively
Drop into a full overhead squat to catch
common_mistakes: Hips hitting the bar out forward
safety: Use bumpers on a platform; reset your back before each rep.
notes: Hang position can be mid-thigh, above knee or below knee.

name: Hang power snatch
form_cues: Lower the bar to mid-thigh with a flat back
Jump and shrug hard
Punch under and catch high with locked arms
safety: Use bumpers and drop the bar forward on a miss.
notes: A great first snatch variation to learn timing and speed.

name: Muscle snatch
form_cues: Extend fully on your toes first
Pull elbows high and out, then turn the bar over
Punch overhead without rebending your knees
safety: Light weights only; it's a technique and upper-back builder.

name: Snatch pull
form_cues: Set up exactly like your snatch
Push the floor away keeping the bar close
Finish fully extended with a shrug, arms straight
safety: Use straps if needed; keep the bar close.
notes: Often done at 90–110% of your best snatch.

name: Snatch high pull
form_cues: Snatch grip, start from floor or hang
Extend fully, then pull elbows high and out
Keep the bar close to your body
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms too early
safety: Control the bar on the way down.

name: Snatch balance
form_cues: Bar on your back with a snatch grip
Dip slightly, then push yourself under the bar fast
Catch in a full overhead squat with locked arms
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar instead of dropping under
safety: Practise bailing; use bumpers and a platform.

name: Squat clean
form_cues: Bar over mid-foot, shoulder-width grip, back flat
Explode through the legs and hips, keeping the bar close
Pull under and catch in a deep front squat
safety: Learn with a coach on a platform with bumpers; drop forward on a miss.

name: Power clean
form_cues: Start like a deadlift with a flat back
Jump when the bar passes your knees
Fast elbows and catch high in a quarter squat
safety: Use bumper plates and a platform.
notes: Popular with athletes for explosive power.

name: Hang clean
form_cues: Start standing, hinge to just above the knees
Explode up and pull under
Catch in a full front squat
safety: Use bumpers; drop forward on a miss.

name: Hang power clean
form_cues: Hinge with the bar at mid-thigh
Jump and shrug
Whip elbows forward and catch above parallel
safety: Bumpers and a clear platform.
notes: Great entry point to Olympic lifting.

name: Clean pull
form_cues: Set up like your clean
Push the floor away and keep the bar close
Finish tall with a strong shrug
safety: Use straps if grip limits you.
notes: Usually loaded at 90–110% of your best clean.

name: Clean high pull
form_cues: Clean grip, start from floor or hang
Extend fully, then drive elbows high
Bar rises close to chest height
safety: Control the lowering.

name: Clean deadlift
form_cues: Set up exactly like your clean
Lift slowly with the chest up and the bar close
Keep shoulders over the bar past the knees
safety: Keep a flat back.
notes: Strength exercise that grooves the first pull of the clean.

name: Clean and jerk
form_cues: Clean the bar to a front squat and stand up
Reset your grip and breath
Dip, drive and split under to lock the bar overhead
safety: Learn from a coach; drop the bar forward on a missed jerk.

name: Split jerk
form_cues: Dip straight down with the bar on your shoulders
Drive up hard, then split your feet
Lock the arms and recover feet together
safety: Use a rack and bumpers; miss forward.

name: Push jerk
form_cues: Dip and drive like a push press
Drop under into a partial squat
Catch with locked arms, then stand
safety: Use a rack and bumpers.

name: Power jerk
form_cues: Dip and drive hard
Jump feet out to squat stance
Catch with locked arms in a quarter squat
safety: Use a rack and bumpers.

name: Push press
form_cues: Bar on front delts, short dip
Drive with the legs
Press to lockout
safety: Use a rack; keep ribs down.

name: Barbell thruster
form_cues: Front-rack the bar
Squat to depth
Drive up and press overhead in one motion
safety: Moderate loads.

name: Sumo deadlift high pull
form_cues: Wide stance, narrow grip
Drive up with legs
Pull elbows high
safety: Moderate loads.

name: Clean and press
form_cues: Power clean to front rack
Stand and brace
Strictly press overhead
safety: Moderate loads.
